name: comp-169
title: Theme Selector Radio
description: Three thumbnail radios show a white, a black and a diagonally split layout preview, captioned Light, Dark and System. The chosen one gains a brighter edge and a tick instead of a dash.
use: In settings, when people should see how light, dark and system modes look before they choose.
avoid: Previews are hand-built mockups, so a custom palette or an extra theme means drawing new artwork.
a11y: Radios stay focusable with a visible ring, but each option is announced twice: the preview image alt and the caption below repeat the same label. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A small heading sits above three short rounded rectangles that mimic a web app with a side rail, header and content blocks: one all white, one all black, one cut corner to corner. Under each rectangle is a tick or a dash with a one-word caption.
behaves: Clicking a rectangle gives it a brighter outline, swaps its dash for a tick and lifts its caption to white. The clip moves Light, Dark, System, then back to Light.
customise: Themes come from an items array; each preview is an inline SVG composed in the file, so its colours are edited there. Captions, values and the tick or dash marks also live in that file.
weight: light: Three small inline SVG thumbnails over native radios with one border fade.
demo: Choose a theme heading; Light, Dark and System previews of a tiny app screen
issues: Each option is read out twice because the preview alt text and the caption carry the same word.
The white Light preview is much brighter than the other two, pulling the eye away from the choice.
polishWhy: Crisp previews and a clear tick state; new themes demand hand-drawn SVG art.
